claims.title: analyze runs analysis over the current repository
claims.claim: Running `truecourse analyze` inside a repository runs static and LLM analysis over that repository and reports the violations it found.
claims.verifyVia: combination: exit code 0 and stdout summarizing the analysis of the current repo
claims.notes: The LLM half is conditional on transport and flags (see the --llm / --no-llm claims); the deterministic half always runs. Restated in the Commands table as 'Analyze current repo'.

claims.title: results are stored as plain JSON under .truecourse/
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze` stores its results as plain JSON files under `.truecourse/` in the analyzed repository.
claims.verifyVia: file: `.truecourse/` exists after the run and contains parseable JSON result files

claims.title: analyze runs the full analysis in-process
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze` runs the full analysis in-process, so it completes with no dashboard or other TrueCourse process running.
claims.verifyVia: exit-code: analyze exits 0 with no server started beforehand
claims.notes: 'in-process' is an implementation detail; the only public observation is that no separate process/daemon has to be started first.

claims.title: list shows the violations analyze found

claims.verifyVia: stdout: violation rows from the latest analysis
claims.notes: Restated in the Commands table as 'Show violations from latest analysis'.

claims.title: analyze --diff diffs the working tree against a committed baseline

claims.notes: Stated fully in baseline-and-diff.mdx; here it is a one-line cross-reference.

claims.title: analyze catches architecture problems

claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Architecture-category violation for code containing one of the listed patterns
claims.notes: The examples are illustrative, not an exhaustive rule list; a scenario proves the category by exercising one named example.

claims.title: analyze catches code-quality problems

claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Code quality violation for code containing one of the listed patterns
claims.notes: Examples are illustrative, not exhaustive.

claims.notes: Examples are illustrative, not exhaustive.

claims.title: analyze catches performance problems

claims.notes: Examples are illustrative, not exhaustive.

claims.title: analyze catches reliability problems

claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Reliability violation for code containing one of the listed patterns
claims.notes: Examples are illustrative, not exhaustive.

claims.title: analyze catches database problems

claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Database violation for code containing one of the listed patterns
claims.notes: Examples are illustrative, not exhaustive.

claims.title: analyze catches style problems

claims.title: deterministic rules cost nothing and make no API calls

claims.title: LLM rules send source code to the configured LLM

claims.notes: Hard to trigger deterministically with real code; the practical setup is to lower TRUECOURSE_DET_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS so an ordinary large file exceeds it.

claims.title: the analysis always completes and writes its output

claims.title: the per-file budget defaults to 30 seconds

claims.verifyVia: stdout: the skip warning or run output reflecting a 30s default when the env override is unset
claims.notes: Only observable by timing unless the CLI prints the budget; a scenario asserting a 30s wall-clock is slow and flaky.

claims.title: TRUECOURSE_DET_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS overrides the per-file budget
claims.claim: Setting `TRUECOURSE_DET_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS` (in milliseconds) overrides the deterministic scan's per-file time budget.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: with the variable set to a very small value, the run emits per-file skip warnings it does not emit at the default

claims.title: hooks install warns and requires confirmation
claims.claim: `truecourse hooks install` warns that commits will take as long as a full diff analysis and requires confirmation before writing the hook.
claims.verifyVia: prompt: a warning plus a confirmation question is shown before anything is written

claims.title: declining the confirmation installs no hook
claims.claim: Declining the `truecourse hooks install` confirmation leaves no pre-commit hook installed.
claims.verifyVia: combination: after declining, a commit that would be blocked completes with no hook output
claims.notes: Implied by 'requires confirmation before writing the hook'; the doc does not describe the decline path explicitly.

claims.title: git commit --no-verify bypasses the hook
claims.claim: `git commit --no-verify` bypasses the pre-commit hook, so a commit that would otherwise be blocked is created.
claims.verifyVia: combination: `git commit --no-verify` exits 0 with no hook output and the commit appears in `git log`

claims.title: hooks install seeds hooks.yaml with starter defaults
claims.claim: `truecourse hooks install` seeds `<repo>/.truecourse/hooks.yaml` with starter defaults.
claims.verifyVia: file: `.truecourse/hooks.yaml` exists after install and contains the documented starter keys

claims.title: the hook reads its policy only from hooks.yaml
claims.claim: The hook reads its policy only from `<repo>/.truecourse/hooks.yaml`, so editing that file changes the hook's behavior.
claims.verifyVia: combination: narrowing `block-on` in hooks.yaml lets a previously blocked commit through

claims.title: a deleted hooks.yaml makes the hook warn
claims.claim: If `hooks.yaml` is deleted, the hook warns on the commit.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a warning about the missing hooks.yaml during `git commit`

claims.title: a deleted hooks.yaml passes every commit
claims.claim: If `hooks.yaml` is deleted, the hook passes every commit rather than applying hidden code-level defaults.
claims.verifyVia: combination: a commit introducing a critical violation exits 0 and appears in `git log`

claims.title: the seeded block-on default is critical and high
claims.claim: The seeded `hooks.yaml` sets `pre-commit.block-on` to `[critical, high]`.
claims.verifyVia: file: the freshly seeded hooks.yaml contains block-on with critical and high
claims.notes: A default value that can drift; also observable through `truecourse hooks status`.

claims.title: block-on accepts the five documented severities
claims.claim: `block-on` accepts the severities info, low, medium, high, and critical.
claims.verifyVia: combination: hooks.yaml configured with each value is accepted and the hook blocks a commit at that severity
claims.notes: The doc lists the valid values but does not state what happens for an invalid one, so the rejection path cannot be claimed.

claims.title: the seeded hooks.yaml disables LLM rules on commit
claims.claim: The seeded `hooks.yaml` sets `pre-commit.llm` to `false`, so the hook's diff analysis runs without LLM rules by default.
claims.verifyVia: combination: the seeded file shows llm false and a commit consumes no LLM tokens

claims.title: setting llm true runs LLM rules on every commit
claims.claim: Setting `pre-commit.llm` to `true` in hooks.yaml makes the hook run LLM rules on every commit, spending tokens per commit.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: the hook's commit output reports LLM usage once llm is true

claims.title: analyze honors .gitignore
claims.claim: Analysis honors the repository's `.gitignore`, so files git ignores are not analyzed.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a violation-bearing file listed in .gitignore produces no violations in `truecourse list`
claims.notes: The doc summarizes the whole rule as 'Anything git ignores, analyze ignores'; the four honored sources are claimed separately.

claims.title: nested .gitignore files are honored
claims.claim: Analysis honors nested `.gitignore` files, not just the one at the repository root.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a violation-bearing file excluded by a subdirectory .gitignore produces no violations

claims.title: .git/info/exclude is honored
claims.claim: Analysis honors `.git/info/exclude`.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a violation-bearing file excluded only via .git/info/exclude produces no violations

claims.title: the configured global excludes file is honored
claims.claim: Analysis honors the user's configured global git excludes file.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a violation-bearing file excluded only via core.excludesFile produces no violations
claims.notes: Requires setting core.excludesFile inside the sandbox; a scenario must not touch the real user-level git config.

claims.title: .truecourseignore excludes tracked paths from analysis
claims.claim: A `.truecourseignore` at the repository root excludes the paths it matches from analysis even though git still tracks them.
claims.verifyVia: combination: the file remains tracked by git while its violations are absent from `truecourse list`

claims.title: .truecourseignore uses .gitignore syntax
claims.claim: `.truecourseignore` uses the same syntax as `.gitignore`, supporting `#` comment lines, directory patterns such as `src/generated/`, and specific file paths such as `scripts/ingest-epub.js`.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a .truecourseignore containing all three documented forms excludes exactly the intended files from `truecourse list`

claims.title: patterns are anchored to the file's location
claims.claim: Patterns are anchored to the location of the `.truecourseignore` file, so `src/generated/` matches only the top-level `src/generated` directory.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a nested `lib/src/generated/` file is still analyzed while the top-level one is not

claims.title: **/ patterns match at any depth
claims.claim: A pattern such as `**/generated/` excludes matching directories at any depth.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: files under both a top-level and a nested generated/ directory are absent from `truecourse list`

claims.title: .truecourseignore also narrows spec scan doc discovery
claims.claim: `.truecourseignore` also narrows spec scan's doc discovery, so markdown it excludes never enters the corpus.
claims.verifyVia: file: after `truecourse spec scan`, the excluded markdown path is absent from `.truecourse/specs/corpus.json`
claims.notes: Cross-capability: the claim lives in the code-analysis docs but is proved through the guard/spec-scan surface, which needs an LLM transport and a full scan run.
